title: Spec 122/123/124 programme backlog — cross-cutting items with no single pilot owner
description: R-T (2026-08-29). Every promise made by Spec 122/123/124 that is NOT owned by one pilot's own nine-commit sequence, declared as data so it is generated and drift-checked rather than re-discovered by a manually-commissioned inventory (docs/reports/generated/122-programme-backlog.md, scripts/violations/generate-programme-backlog.mjs). Mirrors the shape scripts/steps/_schema/converted.json already uses for the same reason: enforcement lives in the artifact, not in memory. x-ruling: R-T.

id.description: Stable id. Reuses the inventory's own id where one exists (e.g. STD-8, LDG-2, VAL-3, PRG-10) so a reader can cross-reference the grounding document; a genuinely new item mints its own (e.g. WD-1, RT-NEW-1).

spec.description: Owning spec number, optionally a section/ruling, e.g. "122 §6.2", "124", "30 §5.4.1", "122 R-D". Starts with the spec number; a second spec cited for context belongs in `promised`/`evidence`, not here — one owning spec per item.

promised.description: Short verbatim or near-verbatim promise text from the owning spec.

evidence.description: A commit hash, a file:line, or a named ruling id. Required for every status — a NOT_STARTED item's evidence is the grep/measurement that PROVES the absence, never empty.

ref.description: kind=pilot -> pilot slug(s); kind=wf/library-wf -> a named WF or "wf: <name>"; kind=followup -> a review_followups.md locator; kind=none -> "" (legal ONLY for status=SUPERSEDED, enforced by the conformance suite, never for NOT_STARTED/PARTIAL).

blocks.description: batching_prereq -> ["batching"]; cutover_prereq -> the specific pilot slug(s) it blocks (e.g. ["refresh_snapshot"]); nice_to_have -> [] (legal only here).

descriptor_path.description: Dot-notation path into the blocked slug's own descriptor JSON (e.g. "recovery.reset").

equals.description: The value descriptor_path must equal for THIS item to actually block the slug. A descriptor whose value differs (or that lacks the path) is not blocked by this item.

applies_when.description: RS-D-STA (2026-09-03, R-T addendum). Optional. Declares that a gate's applicability is itself a fact about the blocked slug's descriptor, not a hand-adjudicated exemption — a programme item authored against a generic archetype-level promise (Spec 120 §6b) before any descriptor of that archetype existed to check it against. Omitted -> the item blocks unconditionally (pre-existing behaviour).

allOf.$comment: RS-D-STA follow-on (2026-09-03, WF1 'state tables reset'). A cutover_prereq normally names the slug(s) it blocks (minItems 1). A FORWARD-DECLARED cutover_prereq — a real requirement with applies_when-declared applicability but ZERO current victims (e.g. STA-1: no descriptor declares outputs.publish:"pointer" yet) — may declare blocks:[] instead, on the condition that applies_when is present: the item is armed the moment a future descriptor's blocks[] entry is added, never silently unenforceable. blocks:[] with no applies_when stays illegal (indistinguishable from a mis-typed nice_to_have).
